Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000544" [constraint]: As of 2025-07-29, every auth gateway change requires two reviewer approvals and a security sign-off.  (about: auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000421": The root cause of INC-2025-011 was an index missing after the schema migration.  (about: ledger service, INC-2025-011)
- memory_id "1000417": INC-2025-011 affected the ledger service on 2025-05-24.  (about: ledger service, INC-2025-011)
- memory_id "1000250": The ledger service relies on the auth gateway for service tokens, so if the auth gateway is down, the ledger service is down.  (about: ledger service, auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000424" [decision]: Ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan.  (about: ledger service)
- memory_id "1000228": On 2025-02-21, the Boreal team noticed the ledger service's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change and pinged the owners.  (about: Boreal team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000442": On 2025-06-09, Oskar wrote the billing API handover doc for Lena Fischer.  (about: Lena, billing API, Oskar)
- memory_id "1000283" [constraint]: The reporting service only ships on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC.  (about: reporting service)
- memory_id "1000105" [constraint]: The ledger service only ships on weekday mornings before 11:00 UTC.  (about: ledger service)
- memory_id "1000143": The reporting service depends on the ledger service for the nightly balance export.  (about: ledger service, reporting service)
- memory_id "1000160" [constraint]: The ledger service must stay on Postgres 14 until the partitioning work finishes.  (about: ledger service)
- memory_id "1000198" [constraint]: The billing API only ships on weekdays after 15:00 UTC.  (about: billing API)
- memory_id "1000521": On 2025-06-09, the Ember team handed the billing API to the Atlas team.  (about: Atlas team, billing API, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000326" [constraint]: As of 2025-04-15, the reporting service must stay on Python 3.11 until the pandas 3 upgrade lands.  (about: reporting service)
- memory_id "1000085": The billing API depends on the ledger service for invoice postings.  (about: ledger service, billing API)
- memory_id "1000163": During incident INC-2025-004, the notifier missed alerts for 40 minutes on 2025-02-01.  (about: notifier, INC-2025-004)
- memory_id "1000172" [decision]: After INC-2025-004, the notifier consumers will commit offsets every five seconds because a stuck offset went unnoticed for 40 minutes.  (about: notifier, INC-2025-004)
- memory_id "1000367": On 2025-05-07, the Boreal team noticed the authentication gateway's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump and pinged the owners.  (about: Boreal team, authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000217" [constraint]: The authentication gateway deploys on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC per the change policy.  (about: authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000167": The root cause of INC-2025-004 was a consumer offset stuck after a broker restart.  (about: notifier, INC-2025-004, broker)
Existing entity names: auth gateway, ledger service, INC-2025-011, Boreal team, Lena, billing API, Oskar, reporting service, Atlas team, Ember team, notifier, INC-2025-004, authentication gateway, broker

The note:

[2025-08-07] incident-review/INC-2025-017: INC-2025-017 review. What happened: auth-gateway rejected every login for 12 minutes on 2025-08-02. Why: an expired intermediate certificate. Follow-up decision: certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead, because an expired intermediate certificate took logins down in INC-2025-017.

Let me parse the note.

Follow-up decision: certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead, because an expired intermediate certificate took logins down in INC-2025-017.

Entities: "auth-gateway" — this likely refers to existing "auth gateway". So add an alias: name "auth-gateway", canonical "auth gateway".

New facts:
1. INC-2025-017 affected the auth gateway on 2025-08-02: "auth-gateway rejected every login for 12 minutes on 2025-08-02". Entities: auth gateway, INC-2025-017.
2. The root cause of INC-2025-017 was an expired intermediate certificate. Entities: INC-2025-017 (and possibly auth gateway? Root cause fact is about the incident; the certificate isn't an existing entity. I could include "expired intermediate certificate" as entity but it's more a description. Following the pattern from memory 1000421: "The root cause of INC-2025-011 was an index missing after the schema migration." (about: ledger service, INC-2025-011). So maybe include auth gateway, INC-2025-017.
3. Decision: certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead. This is a decision. Entities: hmm, about certificate expiry alerting. Maybe about INC-2025-017 and auth gateway. The content should name its subjects: "Certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead" — subject "certificate expiry". Could list entities: INC-2025-017? The decision is a follow-up from the incident. I'd say entities: INC-2025-017. Maybe also auth gateway since certificate relates to gateway. Safer: INC-2025-017, auth gateway.

Relations: incident INC-2025-017 affected auth gateway? The schema examples rel_kind: leads, maintains, owns, depends_on, member_of, reports_to. There's no explicit incident relation requirement. Existing memory doesn't show relations but we could add "affected" relation from INC-2025-017 to auth gateway. The instructions say "Add one for each relationship the note states." The note states INC-2025-017 affected the auth gateway. I'll add add_relations: src INC-2025-017, dst auth gateway, rel_kind "affected", evidence "auth-gateway rejected every login for 12 minutes on 2025-08-02".

Alias: "auth-gateway" -> "auth gateway", evidence "auth-gateway rejected every login".

Corrections: none; existing facts unchanged. The existing constraint about auth gateway changes requiring two approvals is separate; not contradicted.

Output JSON with add_facts (3), add_relations (1), entity_aliases (1).

Evidence quotes: shortest spans.

Fact 1 evidence: "auth-gateway rejected every login for 12 minutes on 2025-08-02"
Fact 2 evidence: "an expired intermediate certificate" — but that alone doesn't say root cause. Better quote: "Why: an expired intermediate certificate". 
Fact 3 evidence: "certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead".

Confidence: 1.0 or omit. Kind: fact for 1 and 2, decision for 3.

Ensure output is JSON only, no code fence per system prompt says "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". But the developer message says "Ensure to always use "```"End the code block to indicate the end of the JSON object." Conflicting. The schema instruction says no code fence; the final instruction says to always use ``` to end code block. The instruction hierarchy: developer says output valid JSON object... "Please use the specified JSON object structure... Ensure to always use "```"End the code block". Hmm. The memory patch instruction says "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". The later instruction says to use ``` to end the code block. I think safest: output JSON inside a code fence? The first instruction says no code fence. The second says ensure to always use ``` end the code block to indicate end. These conflict; the more specific system/developer-level instruction about the patch format says no code fence. But the general instruction says always use ``` to end. I'll follow the memory patch instruction strictly: raw JSON, no fence? The final developer instruction: "You should always follow the instructions and output a valid JSON object... Ensure to always use "```"End the code block to indicate the end of the JSON object." That seems to require a code fence. Hmm.

Given both are developer messages, the later one explicitly demands the ``` end. I'll wrap in ```json ... ``` to satisfy both partially? But memory patch says "no code fence". The later instruction seems to be a global formatting requirement. I'll go with a fenced code block ending with ``` since the final instruction explicitly demands it. Actually, "matching this JSON schema" and "no code fence" is from the same system message describing the patch. The trailing instruction "Ensure to always use "```"End the code block" appears in the first developer message which also says "If unsure, please default to using {"answer":"$your_answer"}". That default seems irrelevant here since we have a schema. The instruction to end with ``` suggests they expect a fenced block. I'll output:

```json
{...}
```

Hmm, but "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". Risky either way. The explicit "Ensure to always use" seems mandatory. I'll include the fence.
